title: Full-Stack PostgreSQL + Prisma + Next.js
description: Build a complete full-stack flow using PostgreSQL, Prisma, Next.js Server Actions, Route Handlers, and authentication.

data.text: This lesson ties together everything you have learned. You will build a complete full-stack feature: a task management app using PostgreSQL, Prisma, Next.js Server Actions, Route Handlers, and session-based authentication.
Start by defining your Prisma schema with User, Task, and Project models. Use relations to connect users to tasks and projects.

data.title: Prisma Schema
data.content: Define the schema for a task management app.

data.text: Create Server Actions for creating tasks, toggling completion, and deleting tasks. Each action uses Prisma to mutate the database.

data.title: Server Actions

data.text: Expose a REST API endpoint for tasks using Route Handlers. This allows external clients or server components to fetch and manipulate tasks.

data.title: Route Handler

data.text: Use Server Actions in client components to create and manage tasks. Use the Route Handler to fetch the task list.

data.title: Client Component
data.content: A client component that displays and manages tasks.

data.text: Use Auth.js to authenticate users. The session is available in Server Actions and Route Handlers, allowing you to associate tasks with the correct user.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prisma schema defines User, Project, and Task models with relations
Server Actions handle mutations (create, toggle, delete)
Route Handlers expose a REST API for fetching tasks
Client components use Server Actions and SWR for data fetching
Auth.js session ties tasks to authenticated users
data.takeaway: This full-stack flow demonstrates how PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Next.js work together to build a production-ready application.
